merger_description:
Laundy Woy Freehold Pty Ltd and Laundy Woy Trading Pty Ltd (**Laundy**) proposes to acquire the business assets, including the freehold land from Amal Trustees Pty Limited as trustee for Harvest Pub Trust 2 and Harvest Pub Operations 2 Limited (**Harvest Pub**) (collectively referred to as the **Parties**).

Laundy proposes to acquire the following businesses in Woy Woy, New South Wales:

* Woy Woy Hotel at 33-39 The Boulevarde, Woy Woy
* An onsite drive-through bottle shop trading as Thirsty Camel

(the**Acquisition**).

Laundy operates a portfolio of hospitality venues across New South Wales and Queensland, specialising in gaming, wagering, bistros, sports bars, retail liquor, entertainment and accommodation. Laundy currently owns and operates the Bayview Hotel located at 2/16, The Boulevarde, Woy Woy, NSW.

The Woy Woy Hotel, operated by Harvest Pub, offers on-premises hospitality services, entertainment, gaming facilities, and an onsite drive-through bottle shop.

The Parties overlap in the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services (including bar service, casual dining and gaming facilities) in the Woy Woy area.

determination_table_content.details:
Laundy Woy Freehold Pty Ltd and Laundy Woy Trading Pty Ltd
(Laundy) proposes to acquire the business assets, including the
freehold land, of the Woy Woy Hotel from Amal Trustees Pty Limited
as trustee for Harvest Pub Trust 2 and Harvest Pub Operations 2
Limited (Harvest Pub) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Laundy operates a portfolio of hospitality venues across New South
Wales and Queensland, specialising in gaming, wagering, bistros,
sports bars, retail liquor, entertainment and accommodation. Laundy
currently owns and operates the Bayview Hotel located at 2/16, The
Boulevarde, Woy Woy, New South Wales.
The Woy Woy Hotel, operated by Harvest Pub, offers on-premises
hospitality services, entertainment, gaming facilities, and an onsite
drive-through bottle shop located at 33-39 The Boulevarde, Woy Woy,
New South Wales.

Laundy and Harvest Pub overlap in the retail supply of on-premises
hospitality services (including bar service, casual dining, gaming
facilities and entertainment) on the Woy Woy peninsula, New South
Wales.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, additional information provided by the parties, and
information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
▪ The Woy Woy Hotel and Bayview Hotel compete closely, having
regard to the on-premises hospitality services offered at each
venue and their geographic proximity to each other.
▪ Post-acquisition, Laundy will continue to face competition from,
and be constrained by, the following venues on the Woy Woy
peninsula:
− the licensed clubs, which provide a strong competitive
constraint in the case of the Woy Woy peninsula, due to
similar service offerings, often at lower price points. In
particular, the Everglades Country Club targets similar
customers and is relatively close to the Woy Woy Hotel and
Bayview Hotel and is a larger venue that was recently
renovated.
− Other hotels and pubs located in Umina Beach and Ettalong
Beach. While Umina Beach and Ettalong Beach venues are
further away, for a high proportion of residents on the
peninsula the travel time to attend the venue will be similar
to the Woy Woy Hotel and Bayview Hotel.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
